input: Pack a hospital bag at thirty-six weeks pregnant

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The bag's contents differ significantly depending on whether it needs to cover just the birthing person, the newborn, a birth partner, or all three — and whether one bag or several are being packed.
Whether a birth partner will be present and staying overnight changes what items need to be included for their comfort and needs.
The type of planned birth (vaginal, scheduled C-section, or unplanned) and the birth setting (hospital, birth centre, home backup) directly determines which supplies are necessary.
Hospital policies vary widely on what they provide (nappies, pads, gowns, formula) versus what must be brought from home, which affects the entire packing list.

Knowing whether the person has started packing at all, or needs a full from-scratch checklist, determines whether the plan should focus on sourcing items, organising existing ones, or just verifying completeness.
Personal priorities — such as comfort items, a birth plan, specific clothing choices, or pain-relief preferences — shape which items are essential versus optional extras.
The desired length of hospital stay (24-hour discharge vs. 3–4 days) significantly changes the volume and variety of items that need to be packed.

gold.taskTitle: Pack a hospital bag at 36 weeks pregnant
gold.taskDescription: Prepare a fully packed hospital bag with everything needed for labour, delivery, and the postpartum stay before the 36-week mark.

questions.title: Who are you packing the bag for — just yourself, baby, birth partner, or all three?
questions.description: Identify whether one combined bag or separate bags are needed, and which people's items must be accounted for.

questions.title: Will a birth partner be staying with you throughout labour and overnight?
questions.description: Determine whether a birth partner's overnight comfort items (snacks, change of clothes, toiletries) need to be included in the plan.

questions.title: What type of birth are you planning — vaginal, scheduled C-section, or unsure?
questions.description: Tailor the packing list to the specific physical recovery needs and likely procedures associated with each birth type.

questions.title: What does your hospital or birth centre already provide on the ward?
questions.description: Avoid duplicating items the hospital supplies (e.g., nappies, maternity pads, formula, gowns) so the bag stays lean and relevant.

questions.title: Have you started packing, or do you need a full from-scratch checklist?
questions.description: Establish the starting point so the plan either builds a complete list or focuses on reviewing and filling gaps in what is already packed.

questions.title: Are there specific comfort, cultural, or personal items you know you want included?
questions.description: Capture high-priority personal preferences such as a birth plan document, specific snacks, music, religious items, or preferred clothing.

questions.title: How long a hospital stay are you expecting after the birth?
questions.description: Adjust the quantity of clothing, toiletries, and supplies based on whether the stay is likely to be 24 hours, 2–3 days, or longer.
